input.question: why haven't we evolved stronger teeth?
input.ground_truth: If our teeth were not good enough to hang in while we bred and raised our young until they were self-sufficient, we would have developed better teeth. Evolutionary adaptations don't happen because it helps us survive. It happens because it helps us live long enough to reproduce and take care of our offspring until *our offspring* can survive. tl;dr: your teeth last until your DNA is done with you.

Okay! Imagine your teeth are like the tools you use to eat your favorite snacks. Over a looong, looong time, our bodies and our teeth have changed a little bit with every generation, kind of like how your toy collection changes as you grow up.

We haven’t grown super strong teeth because we don’t need *super* strong teeth for the kinds of food we eat now. A long time ago, our ancestors ate really tough things, like roots and nuts, so their teeth got bigger and stronger. But now, we eat softer foods like bread, pasta, and fruits. Our bodies don’t need to work as hard to chew, so our teeth don’t have to be as strong.

Also, we take care of our teeth with things like toothbrushes and dentists, which helps them stay healthy even if they’re not super tough.

So, our teeth are just right for the food we eat today!
